children: OTTAWA--Citing strong demand, BCE's chief executive said Monday the company intends to quadruple capacity at a planned artificial-intelligence data center in the western Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

CEO Mirko Bibic unveiled the plan at an investment summit in Toronto, hosted by Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to drum up foreign interest in shovel-ready projects covering energy, mining, manufacturing and power generation.
The company said the total capital investment now associated with this expanded project could exceed 50 billion Canadian dollars ($36.05 billion).

Bibic, at the event alongside Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, said that "the demand signals" were strong, and approached Saskatchewan officials about and expansion. "This reflects a significant stage in the most ambitious digital infrastructure project in Canada," the CEO said.

The project was unveiled this past March, with a capacity for 300 megawatts. With the expansion, that power total climbs to 1.2 gigawatts. One gigawatt is generally enough power to provide electricity to 750,000 homes.
